issues.description: The manuscript provides three different timelines for when the intervention occurs. In the Introduction, it states the warning is placed after collaborative recall. At the end of the Introduction, it states it is placed before collaborative recall to 'inoculate' participants. In the Procedure section, it is listed as Phase 3, occurring after collaborative recall (Phase 2). This makes the experimental design impossible to verify.
issues.quote: In the present study we decided to place the warning after the collaborative recall... [vs] we decided to place the methods inducing resistance to misinformation before the collaborative recall phase... [vs] (2) collaborative recall... (3) three procedures to reduce vulnerability.

issues.description: The analysis plan first states that the study will use open-ended questions as a modification of previous research, but then explicitly states the test will use a two-alternative forced-choice (2AFC) format. These are fundamentally different measurement scales.
issues.quote: modification concerning applying open-ended questions in the individual memory test... [vs] In the present research, the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format.

issues.description: The authors acknowledge that for a small effect size (f = .10), a sample of 664 is required. However, they proceed with N=240. Interactions in ANOVA typically require much larger samples than main effects, and assuming a medium effect size for a novel behavioral intervention is risky and likely over-optimistic.
issues.quote: the required sample sizes for the small, medium, and large effects were 664, 112, and 48 participants, respectively... a sample of 240 participants was assumed.

issues.description: The power analysis assumes a correlation of r = 0.07 between repeated measures. In memory research, the correlation between performance on different item types for the same participant is typically much higher (r > 0.5). An erroneously low correlation estimate significantly biases the power calculation for within-subjects factors.
issues.quote: A correlation r = 0.07 between repeated measures was assumed based on the research described above.

issues.description: The 'Demonstration' group uses the DRM paradigm to show memory fallibility. However, DRM measures internal associative illusions (semantic spreading activation), whereas the MORI task measures external misinformation/social conformity. Susceptibility to one does not necessarily predict or demonstrate susceptibility to the other, undermining the 'demonstration' effect.
issues.quote: the demonstration of the fallibility of memory will be done by means of the DRM technique

issues.description: The authors claim normative impact is 'completely ruled out' because the final test is individual. This ignores the possibility of 'private acceptance' or 'memory commitment' where social pressure during the discussion phase leads to the internal encoding of the partner's error, which then persists in private testing.
issues.quote: we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect is completely ruled out in this study: participants work on their own and do not compare their answers with anybody

issues.description: The control group listens to a podcast on 'soft skills.' This is not an active control for the 'Education' or 'Warning' groups. A proper control should involve a neutral podcast about memory or a general science topic to control for the effects of listening to a 7-minute educational recording.
issues.quote: In the control group, participants will listen to a podcast concerning soft skills related to social attitudes.

issues.description: The authors plan to use ANOVA on the 'number of correct answers' and 'number of misinformation answers.' These are count data (0-8 range), which often violate the normality and homoscedasticity assumptions of ANOVA. Poisson or negative binomial regression would be more appropriate.
issues.quote: We will explore the individual memory test’s scores for the critical details using analysis of variance (ANOVA), using all four indices: the number of correct answers, number of answers consistent with misinformation...

issues.description: The authors list 'other answers' (consistent neither with movie nor misinformation) as one of the four indices. However, if the test is 2-alternative forced-choice (as stated later), 'other' answers are mathematically impossible.
issues.quote: (3) other answers (consistent neither with the movie nor the misinformation)... In the present research, the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format.

issues.description: There is no mention of Institutional Review Board (IRB) approval or ethical considerations, which is critical given the use of deception (MORI technique) and the 'fooling' of participants in the DRM task.
issues.quote: The participants will be debriefed. One experimental session will last about 60 minutes.

issues.description: The sample is restricted to 16-35 year olds. While this controls for age-related memory decline, it severely limits the generalizability of the findings to older adults, who are a significant demographic in actual eyewitness testimony.
issues.quote: The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old

issues.description: The 'Demonstration and Motivation' group is told 'If so, you were fooled.' This aggressive feedback, combined with a lecture on the 'devastating consequences' of errors, may induce strong demand characteristics where participants try to please the experimenter rather than reporting their actual memory.
issues.quote: If so, you were fooled... The devastating consequences of errors caused by the fallibility of memory will be demonstrated.

issues.description: The authors plan to record what participants think the 'real purpose' of the study was but do not provide a specific plan for how to handle participants who correctly identify the deception or the hypothesis.
issues.quote: Their responses will be recorded for exploratory analysis of any relationship between hypothesis awareness and performance.

issues.description: Despite referencing a 'registered report' by Kękuś et al. (2020), the authors do not state whether this specific study is pre-registered, which is standard for modern experimental psychology to prevent p-hacking.
issues.quote: The main goal of this proposal is to analyze the efficacy of three possible methods

issues.description: The MORI technique relies on participants not noticing the duality of the projection. The study lacks a formal manipulation check to ensure participants actually saw different versions and didn't notice the 'ghosting' or overlap of the two images.
issues.quote: the participants sit beside each other, look at the same screen, and are not aware that the other person is watching a different version.

issues.description: Inoculation theory (McGuire) requires exposing the subject to a 'weakened dose' of the persuasive message. The DRM task is not a weakened dose of co-witness misinformation; it is a different cognitive phenomenon. The intervention is more akin to a 'warning' than 'inoculation.'
issues.quote: Their technique was based on the inoculation theory... demonstrating individual vulnerability to influence

issues.description: The analysis plan involves four different dependent variables (indices) and multiple follow-up comparisons between four groups. There is no mention of alpha correction (e.g., Bonferroni) to control for the family-wise error rate.
issues.quote: follow-up comparisons between pairs of groups will be performed.

issues.description: The 15-minute logic puzzle filler task is cognitively demanding. This may induce ego depletion or cognitive fatigue, which could interact with the subsequent interventions and the memory test in ways not accounted for by the design.
issues.quote: the participants will be engaged in a filler task (solving logic puzzles) for 15 minutes.

issues.description: The materials were translated into Polish by a 'native speaker,' but there is no mention of back-translation or validation to ensure the critical details and nuances of the misinformation were preserved.
issues.quote: the instruction was translated into Polish by a native speaker

issues.description: The authors used a random-effects model for a meta-analysis of only two studies to determine effect size. Random-effects models are notoriously unreliable with very small numbers of studies (k < 5), often leading to inaccurate estimates of the mean effect.
issues.quote: random effects were assumed while calculating the joint effect size, which was 1.13.

issues.description: The collaborative recall phase allows participants to document 'both responses' if they disagree. The authors do not specify how this lack of consensus will be coded in the final analysis of 'misleading' items, which could introduce noise into the independent variable.
issues.quote: If the participants are unable to reach an agreement, both responses will be documented.

issues.description: The authors do not specify which 4 critical details (out of the 8 available in the Eric the Electrician video) will be used for the discussion, nor how they were selected. This prevents exact replication.
issues.quote: each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase.

issues.description: A 7-minute podcast is a very brief intervention to expect a change in fundamental metacognitive processes or 'The Seven Sins of Memory.' The construct of 'Education' is weakly operationalized here.
issues.quote: Education about memory will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast

issues.description: The authors state that if a partner guesses the correct answer (consistent with the participant's view), it is not classified as misleading. However, the analysis plan later says they will categorize *all* discussed items as containing misinformation. These statements are contradictory.
issues.quote: if the partner provided an answer consistent with what the participant had seen... the situation will not be classified as misleading... [vs] we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation
